question: Can all objects of this kind be organized into a complete description?
idea: A classification aims to describe every object satisfying specified conditions, rather than just produce a few examples. The assumptions define which objects belong in the collection. This entry states a particular classification claim.
why: The study of shapes defined by equations, often using complex numbers. It connects geometric features with algebraic rules.

glossary.meaning: A particular kind of complex geometric surface with strong symmetry in its geometric structure.
A geometric setting that includes points at infinity, making many geometric relationships more uniform.
A mathematical condition that rules out certain forms of escaping to infinity; in ordinary Euclidean space it means closed and bounded.
A description of all objects of a specified kind, usually organized into recognizable types.
A way of measuring the number of independent directions or degrees of freedom; different theories use different notions.

exactClaim: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces. More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka; a connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII is Oka exactly when it is a Hopf or Enoki surface.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
